classification.difficultyReason: Combine perpendicular gradients, point–gradient equations and simultaneous equations with a parameter.

content.prompt: A line with gradient $-2$ passes through the point $(r,-3)$. A second line, perpendicular to the first, meets this line at the point $(a,b)$. The second line passes through the point $(6,r)$. Find $a$ and $b$ in terms of $r$.

answer.short:
$a=\dfrac{2r}{5}$, $b=\dfrac{6r}{5}-3$.

Use perpendicular gradients to form the two line equations, then solve them simultaneously.
answer.worked:
The second line has gradient $\tfrac12$, since perpendicular gradients have product $-1$.

For the first line:
$$\begin{align*}y+3&=-2(x-r)\\y&=-2x+2r-3\end{align*}$$
For the second line:
$$\begin{align*}y-r&=\tfrac12(x-6)\\y&=\tfrac12x+r-3\end{align*}$$
At their intersection $(a,b)$, equate the expressions for $y$:
$$\begin{align*}-2a+2r-3&=\tfrac12a+r-3\\r&=\tfrac52a\\a&=\tfrac{2r}{5}\end{align*}$$
Substitute into the second line:
$$\begin{align*}b&=\tfrac12\left(\tfrac{2r}{5}\right)+r-3\\b&=\tfrac{6r}{5}-3\end{align*}$$
